english: Let $P(x)=(x+2)(x+1)(2x-1)(x-3)$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Then the sum of all the real roots of the equation $P'(x)+2P(x)=0$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $P(x)=(x+2)(x+1)(2x-1)(x-3)$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$। तब समीकरण $P'(x)+2P(x)=0$ के सभी वास्तविक मूलों का योग ______ है।
solution: $h$ vanishes at $-2,-1,\frac12,3$; Rolle's theorem on $[-2,-1]$, $\left[-1,\frac12\right]$, $\left[\frac12,3\right]$ gives three real roots of $Q$.
$Q(-2)=P'(-2)=(-1)(-5)(-5)=-25<0$ and $Q(x)\to+\infty$ as $x\to-\infty$, so by the IVT $Q$ has a fourth real root in $(-\infty,-2)$.
solution_full: Let $h(x)=e^{2x}P(x)$. Then $h'(x)=e^{2x}\left(P'(x)+2P(x)\right)=e^{2x}Q(x)$, and $e^{2x}>0$, so the roots of $Q$ are exactly the roots of $h'$.

$h$ is differentiable and $h(-2)=h(-1)=h\left(\frac12\right)=h(3)=0$. Rolle's theorem on $[-2,-1]$, $\left[-1,\frac12\right]$ and $\left[\frac12,3\right]$ gives roots of $Q$ in $(-2,-1)$, $\left(-1,\frac12\right)$ and $\left(\frac12,3\right)$: three distinct real roots.

Fourth root: $Q(-2)=P'(-2)+2P(-2)=P'(-2)$. Since $P'(-2)=(-2+1)(2(-2)-1)(-2-3)=(-1)(-5)(-5)=-25$ (the other terms of the product rule vanish at the root $-2$), $Q(-2)=-25<0$. Also $Q(x)\to+\infty$ as $x\to-\infty$. By the intermediate value theorem $Q$ has a root in $(-\infty,-2)$.
So $Q$ has four distinct real roots, one in each of $(-\infty,-2)$, $(-2,-1)$, $\left(-1,\frac12\right)$, $\left(\frac12,3\right)$, and these are all its roots.
The sum of all real roots is therefore the sum of all roots: $-\dfrac{6}{4}=-1.5$ (numerically the roots are about $-2.966$, $-1.358$, $0.163$, $2.661$).
originality_note: New: the roots of P' + 2P are located by Rolle on e^{2x}P and the missing fourth root by the IVT, so that 'sum of real roots' equals the Vieta sum (way 5). Closest known: between two roots of f lies a root of f' + lambda f (Rolle on e^{lambda x} f). Different because: the question asks for a sum that is only computable after proving all four roots are real, and the fourth root lies outside the span of the roots of P.

concept_use.Rolle's theorem and its application: Rolle on h(x) = e^{2x}P(x) between consecutive roots of P gives three real roots of P' + 2P.
concept_use.Intermediate Value theorem: Q(-2) = -25 < 0 and Q -> +infinity as x -> -infinity give the fourth real root in (-infinity, -2).

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, curve and function introduced with its domain; conditions complete; one reading of each sentence; answer unique and equal to the plan (negative decimal); Hindi mirrors the English maths. All four roots real, so 'sum of all real roots' is the Vieta sum. No change.
key_step: Recognise P' + 2P as e^{-2x}(e^{2x}P)', apply Rolle three times and the IVT once to show all four roots are real.
justification: Two ideas linked (Rolle on an auxiliary function, then IVT for the remaining root) before a Vieta finish; the hidden auxiliary function is a known coaching trick, so 3 rather than 4, compared with 2023-P2-Q7 (L3).
